newsitem.title: USA: Firefighters set to contain California wildfire.
newsitem.headline: Firefighters set to contain California wildfire.

text.p: Firefighters battled on Tuesday to contain fully a stubborn wildfire in California's scenic Los Padres National Forest, officials said.
The fire, which has charred 21,800 acres (8,700 hectares) of trees and brush, was 95 percent contained and full containment was expected by Tuesday evening.
"It has been a difficult fire to fight," said Jim Youngson, a spokesman for the U.S. Forest Service. "This fire took a lot of patience on behalf of firefighters."

The fire was burning in steep, rugged terrain just south of Big Sur, a popular hiking and camping area on the central California coast. The cause of the blaze, which broke out a week ago about 150 miles (240 km) south of San Francisco, has been confirmed as arson.

Firefighters have made good progress over the last few days, officials said. But the fire has increased sharply in size since Monday because firefighters were burning nearby vegetation to make the blaze easier to control.
As of early Tuesday, 2,092 firefighters were still battling the blaze, backed by 93 fire engines, five air tankers, nine helicopters and 11 bulldozers.
Five homes and nine outbuildings have been destroyed. Fire officials said no other homes were immediately threatened.
Six firefighters have been injured battling the blaze, the officials said.
